candidates.label: Sardis archaeological site (Sart)
candidates.support: The extensively excavated site near modern Sart is undisputed as ancient Sardis, capital of the Kingdom of Lydia; Pleiades and Wikidata's coordinates for the site agree closely.

summary.text: Sardis was the capital of the ancient Kingdom of Lydia and, per World History Encyclopedia, was known in antiquity for its wealth and culture and for its favorable position on a major trade route between the Aegean coast and the interior of Asia Minor, later becoming an important city of the Roman province of Asia. It is one of the seven churches addressed in Revelation 2-3, warned there, 'I know your works, that you have a reputation of being alive, but you are dead.'

history.text: Sardis was capital of the Lydian kingdom under kings such as Croesus, famed for his wealth, until the Persian conquest of 547/546 BC; it later passed through Seleucid and Roman rule, remained an important city of Roman Asia, and by the 7th century had long been associated with Christianity as one of the seven churches of Revelation.

scripture.textWEB: saying, “What you see, write in a book and send to the seven assemblies: to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and to Laodicea.”

“And to the angel of the assembly in Sardis write: “He who has the seven Spirits of God and the seven stars says these things: “I know your works, that you have a reputation of being alive, but you are dead.
Nevertheless you have a few names in Sardis that didn’t defile their garments. They will walk with me in white, for they are worthy.
